name: Topology: shape without size
description: Distance, open sets, continuity, surfaces and loops: the shape of things that can stretch and bend, taught at the Kepler outpost.
about:
Topology realm ("Topology: shape without size"): distance, open and closed sets, continuity, connectedness, compactness,
surfaces, curvature and loops, for an adult who has finished Foundations, Calculus 1 and 2, Logic and proof and Real analysis.
Same Kepler outpost, now the Shape Lab, where the crew builds domes, cable looms and hull panels whose shape matters more than
their size. Mira is still the mentor. The concept plan is docs/plans/TOPO-PLAN.md.

mentor.name: Mira
mentor.opening: I’m Mira. Every cable, panel and dome in the Shape Lab changes its measurements when we bend it, and we have to {purpose}. Your task is “{title}.” {brief} The idea we need: {topic}.
mentor.closing: You already have everything this needs from Foundations, Calculus and Real analysis. I’ll work the first example with you, and the guided steps are there whenever you want them.

copy.homeTitle:
Stretch it, bend it, it stays the same.
Learn what shape really means.
copy.firstVisit: Welcome to the Shape Lab. Our domes inflate, our cables bend and our hull panels stretch, so the measurements we used to trust keep changing. We start with the question underneath all of it: what does it mean for two places to be close?
copy.allDone: You can now name every hull we could ever sew and count every loop round the ring. Complex analysis opens next at the Antenna Field, where winding numbers turn into integrals.
copy.chaptersNote: Seven chapters. Learn every concept in a chapter to unlock a landmark for the outpost. Practice missions are optional.

skills.title: The skill tree
skills.text: Follow the prerequisite branches from distance to loops. Each mission you finish opens the ideas that are built on it.

visual.title: The concept bench
visual.text: Pick any mission, change its numbers and predict the answer before you check it. Nothing here affects your progress, and it all works offline.

help.title: Look for what stays the same when you stretch.
help.intro: Topology starts where real analysis ends: with a set of places and a way of saying which ones are near. It studies the shape of things that can be stretched, bent and glued but not torn. Every new word and symbol is explained before you are asked to use it, with a worked example first.
help.answers: Answers are numbers: a distance, a radius, a count, an Euler characteristic, a genus, a winding number, an area or a curvature. A shape is never typed. A yes or no is typed as 1 or 0. Decimals are given to 2 places unless a mission says otherwise.
